scope: all client-facing LaTeX-generated agreements, quotations, letters, reports and payment papers
all externally circulated PDF or rendered text
rule: Internal IDs, review statuses, AI/database implementation terminology and machine-oriented project names must not be visible in client-facing LaTeX documents or compiled PDFs. Keep these details in private input schemas, filenames, comments, logs, registries, QA evidence and source lineage. Use human-friendly document titles, project names and business references in visible text. Fail closed rather than silently changing an actual client's name or omitting contractual provisions.
exceptions: Business construction terms, such as MS railing, uPVC and safe demolition methods, remain allowed. This policy does not forbid computer systems from being used privately to build, validate and preserve source files.
gates: scan visible fields before LaTeX interpolation
verify projected visible LaTeX after generation
compile with immutable approved canonical v3 template and private brand overlay
run human visual QA and other legal/technical gates
output_status_rule: No user-facing document may claim legal or commercial approval from a successful compilation test.
public_private_boundary: Public repository contains only generic blank source and policy, never client contract values or signatures.

required: input fields used in visible headings/body/tables
rendered client-facing LaTeX body after placeholder resolution
allowed_internal: PDF filenames and internal audit records
scanning_scope.historical_exception: Existing immutable historical sources and fictional legacy regression output are preserved but are not client-ready; no retroactive rewrite or silent certification

release_rule: Client-visible source or PDF lint failure blocks delivery. Passing lint is NOT legal, engineering, financial, design or human approval.
